summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted after being found down at home with weakness, hypoglycemia, and signs of systemic infection. He was diagnosed with methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA) bacteremia originating from his tunneled hemodialysis catheter, which was removed. He developed septic pulmonary emboli and multiple lung abscesses, requiring ICU admission, mechanical ventilation after a seizure, and broad-spectrum antibiotics. The infection source was confirmed by positive catheter tip and blood cultures. He was transitioned from vancomycin to nafcillin and later to cefazolin for outpatient therapy. A temporary femoral dialysis catheter was placed due to central venous obstruction, later replaced with a tunneled femoral catheter. He gradually improved, was extubated, and regained strength. He was discharged to an extended care facility for continued IV antibiotics, dialysis, and physical therapy, with plans to follow up on a renal cyst and thyroid enlargement.
problems: Other and unspecified infection due to central venous catheter
